hkg_007: You can recognise it as a fig growing out of a stone retaining wall, maintained by the department that looks after masonry rather than parks. It stands in the Ka Wai Man Road Garden, Kennedy Town.
hkg_010: You can recognise it by its crown, spreading 22 metres over one of Hong Kong's busiest streets, cabled and braced for support. It stands on the Park Lane Shopper's Boulevard, Nathan Road, opposite St Andrew's Church.
szb_007: You can recognise it by its multiple trunks rising from one base, visible from all sides at the property edge. It stands at the junction of Neutorstrasse, Hubnergasse and Leopoldskronstrasse, Riedenburg.
szb_008: You can recognise it as the lime that once stood inside the grounds of the Molckhof manor house. It stands on Gartnerstrasse, near the Molckhof, Riedenburg.
com_004: You can recognise it by its crown, turning butter gold across the whole tree at once each November and dropping within days, with none of the smell a female ginkgo would leave. It stands over a lakeside clearing on Viale Geno.
com_008: You can recognise it by its trunk, 4.3 metres round, standing in the middle of the square where Como's traffic converges. It stands in Piazzale Camerlata.
cbr_002: You can recognise it as the tallest tree in Europe, somewhere between 73 and 75 metres depending on who measured it. It stands in the Mata Nacional de Vale de Canas, a quarter hour's walk from the car park.
cbr_003: You can recognise it by its mast-like trunk, the tallest bunya pine recorded in Portugal, standing a few dozen metres from the Karri Knight on the same path. It stands in the Mata Nacional de Vale de Canas.
ass_002: You can recognise it by the cavity opened along its north side by decades of sulfur polypore fungus, still standing despite it. It stands a short walk from Overcingel's horse chestnut on the same estate.
ass_006: You can recognise it by its branches, arching outward and down instead of up, in a pocket garden with a pond at its centre. It stands behind Nieuw Echten, reached only by the footpath between numbers 59 and 61 Alteveerstraat.
rog_001: You can recognise it as the undated of Rogalin's three named oaks, 6.33 metres round, ninety metres from its dated neighbour Rus. It stands in the parkland by Rogalin Palace.
rog_002: You can recognise it as the thickest of Rogalin's oaks, 9.15 metres round and tree-ring dated to 800 to 850 years, the oldest oak dated anywhere in Poland. It stands in the parkland by Rogalin Palace.
